page.emptyBody: In “Measure”, drag on a chart to pick a range, then press “Analyze the range”. From the “Notebook” you can send a whole measurement.

box.name: Panel name
box.deleteDesc: The original measurement stays in the Notebook.

select.title: Range
select.text: Drag on the chart to pick part of the data: mean, spread and change update as you go.

line.title: Line by eye
line.text: Draw by hand the line that best follows the points, then measure its slope with two points.

tangent.title: Tangent
tangent.text: Slope of the curve at a point, for example the velocity at an instant. Tap a point on the chart.

fit.title: Fit
fit.text: Curve closest to the points (least squares), with parameters and uncertainties. Drag on the chart to restrict it to a range.

ruler.title: Ruler
ruler.text: Period of a wave: move the two lines onto two crests and enter how many periods lie between them.

result.statsDetail: {n, plural, one {# point} other {# points}}; s = {sd} {unit}; min {min}, max {max}; Δ{y}/Δ{x} = {rate} {su}
result.tangentDetail: P = ({x}, {y}); parabola through the {n} nearest points
result.fitDetail: {n, plural, one {# point} other {# points}}, {t1}–{t2} {unit}; R² = {r2}

eye.drag: Drag the green circles until the line runs through the middle of the points: as many above as below.
eye.pickTwo: Tap two points on the line, far apart.

tangent.tap: Tap a point on the curve.
tangent.needThree: At least 3 nearby points are needed.
tangent.how: Measured data have no formula: take the {n} points closest to P and compute the parabola that best approximates them. The tangent is the line that touches that parabola at P. The triangle shows the slope: how much {y} changes when {x} increases by {dx} {unit}.

fit.spread: Typical deviation of the points from the curve: {s} {unit} · {n, plural, one {# point} other {# points}} · {t1}–{t2} {xunit}
fit.unc1: Standard deviation of the data, s = {s} {unit}: the typical deviation of the points from the curve. It is computed from the residuals r (data − curve): s = √( Σr² / (n − p) ), with n points and p parameters.
fit.unc2: Standard uncertainty of a parameter: the number after the ±. It grows with s and shrinks with the number of points and how widely they are spread.
fit.uncLine: For the slope: σₘ = s / √Σ({x} − {x}̄)², so a longer stretch along the horizontal axis gives a more precise slope.
fit.uncNonlin: In non-linear models it is derived from the same s, weighted by how much each parameter moves the curve.
fit.unc3: The line by eye applies the same idea by hand: compare the two results.
fit.r2Body: R² is the fraction of the variation in the data explained by the model: 1 if all the points lie on the curve, 0 if the model explains nothing. A high R² does not prove the model is right (a line over part of a parabola can give R² = 0.99): that is why you check the residuals.

resid.title: Residuals = data − model
resid.systematic: ✗ Systematic residuals: they change sign {runs} times versus about {mu} expected for random data. The points form a “belly” relative to the curve: the model does not describe this range. Change the model or the range.
resid.random: ✓ Random residuals around zero: they change sign {runs} times, about the {mu} expected. The model is adequate for this range.
resid.tooFew: Too few points to assess the residuals.
resid.how: With the right model each point falls above or below the curve at random, like tossing a coin, and the sign of the residuals changes often. With the wrong model you see long stretches all above and then all below. The sign changes are counted and compared with those expected by chance (Wald–Wolfowitz runs test): the verdict is negative if they are more than 2 standard deviations below the expected number.

ruler.peaks: Put the lines on two peaks and count the intervals between them.
ruler.crests: Put the lines on two matching points of the wave (two crests) and count the periods between them.
ruler.precision: The more periods you span, the more precise the measurement: the reading error is divided by N.

stats.needTwo: At least 2 points are needed. Drag on the chart to pick a range.
stats.selected: Range {a} – {b} {unit} · {n, plural, one {# point} other {# points}}
stats.meanHint: ± = standard error of the mean, s/√n
stats.sdHint: typical deviation of the individual values from the mean
stats.changeHint: last value − first value of the range
stats.whyTitle: Mean, s and standard error of the mean
stats.why1: s is the typical deviation of the individual values from the mean. The standard error of the mean (the number after the ±) is s/√n: with more points the mean is more precise, even if each value fluctuates as much as before.
stats.why2: Use the mean over a range where the quantity stays constant, such as an equilibrium temperature or a position at rest.

compare.footer: The best model has the smallest s and random residuals. If results are similar, choose the simplest one with a physical meaning. Tap a row to use it.
